'''Aron Kuppermann''' (May 6, 1926 &ndash; October 14, 2011) was a professor of chemical physics at [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1021/jp004063f | title = Autobiographical Notes of Aron Kuppermann† | year = 2001 | journal = The Journal of Physical Chemistry A | volume = 105 | pages = 2129–2131 | issue = 11| bibcode = 2001JPCA..105.2129. }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1021/jp010296a | title = Tribute to Aron Kuppermann† | year = 2001 | journal = The Journal of Physical Chemistry A | volume = 105 | pages = 2127–2128 | issue = 11| bibcode = 2001JPCA..105.2127. }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Cohen|first1=Shirley K.|title=Interview with Aron Kuppermann: California Institute of Technology Archives Oral History Project|url=http://oralhistories.library.caltech.edu/208/10/Kuppermann%20OHO.pdf|publisher=California Institute of Technology|access-date=29 November 2017|date=2012}}</ref> The author of more than 200 publications, he is perhaps best known for his work in the application of quantum mechanics to the solution of problems in chemical reaction dynamics and kinetics.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Fesenmaier|first1=Kimm|title=Aron Kuppermann, 85|date=18 October 2011 |url=https://www.caltech.edu/news/aron-kuppermann-85-1994|publisher=California institute of Technology|access-date=29 November 2017}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite journal|last1=Schatz|first1=George|last2=Kuppermann|first2=Aron|title=Quantum mechanical reactive scattering for three-dimensional atom plus diatom systems. I. Theory|journal=Journal of Chemical Physics|date=1976|volume=65|issue=11|page=4642|doi=10.1063/1.432918|bibcode=1976JChPh..65.4642S|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/33014/1/SCHAjcp76b.pdf}}</ref> Kuppermann and [[George C. Schatz|George Schatz]] completed the first calculation of the dynamics of a chemical reaction in a full 3-dimensional quantum model.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jta.org/2011/10/24/news-opinion/obituaries/aron-kuppermann-leading-chemical-physicist-dies-at-85|title=Aron Kuppermann, leading chemical physicist, dies at 85 {{!}} Jewish Telegraphic Agency|website=www.jta.org|date=24 October 2011 |language=en-US|access-date=2018-07-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schatz|first1=George C.|last2=Kuppermann|first2=Aron|date=1976|title=Quantum mechanical reactive scattering for three-dimensional atom plus diatom systems. II. Accurate cross sections for H+H2|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|language=en|volume=65|issue=11|pages=4668–4692|doi=10.1063/1.432919|issn=0021-9606|bibcode=1976JChPh..65.4668S|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/33019/1/SCHAjcp76c.pdf}}</ref>

Born in Brazil, Kuppermann earned degrees in [[Chemical engineering|Chemical Engineering]] (1948) and [[Civil engineering|Civil Engineering]] (1952) from the [[University of São Paulo]]. He served as an assistant professor of chemistry at the [[Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica]] in [[São José dos Campos]] (1950–51). He was a [[British Council]] Scholar at the [[University of Edinburgh]], [[Scotland]] in 1953, and earned a Ph.D. in physical chemistry at the [[University of Notre Dame]] in 1955. He then joined the faculty of the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]] (1955–1963) and subsequently came to [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1963.

==Awards and recognitions==

Kuppermann received the Centennial of Science Award from Notre Dame in 1965. In 1967 he was the Venable Lecturer at the University of North Carolina, and in 1968 was named the Werner Lecturer at the University of Kansas. He was the Kolthoff Lecturer at the University of Minnesota in 1984. He was a John Simon Guggenheim Fellow at the Weizmann Institute and the University of São Paulo in 1976 and 1977.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cce.caltech.edu/faculty/kuppermann/cv.html |title=Aron Kuppermann Professor of Chemical Physics Curriculum Vitae |publisher=California Institute of Technology |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100608045347/http://www.cce.caltech.edu/faculty/kuppermann/cv.html |archivedate=2010-06-08 }}</ref>
